correctness.rationale: For each cycle, full visitation occurs at the first lifted range of length n-1; this is an exact elementary equivalence. Positive drift gives an attained finite global minimum and finite maximum before its first occurrence, producing simultaneous almost-sure eventual equality T_n=H_{n-1-J} and L_n=n-1-J for all large n. The negative minimum is geometric by a two-barrier gambler-ruin limit. Strong-Markov first-passage increments are iid with mean 1/(p-q) and variance 4pq/(p-q)^3, giving the CLT; the random fixed shift costs O_P(1). The joint independence argument conditions on a fixed finite initial path, applies the future passage-time CLT, then approximates the eventual global minimum by the finite-prefix minimum. All quantifiers fixed p>1/2 are explicit. Finite code reproduced 26859 exact or pathwise checks, not used as proof of infinite claims.

value.rationale: The random final surveillance location and time to complete a biased cycle are operationally coupled observables. The theorem gives more than their classical separate limits: a sample-path invariant shared by all sufficiently large ring sizes, an eventual exact cover-time-to-hitting-time reduction, and asymptotic independence of an O(1) geometric location defect and O(sqrt(n)) Gaussian completion-time noise. This resolves a natural joint-observable gap motivated by the explicit cover-time and terminal-concentration questions in the new cycle study; the strong coupling is a reusable structural tool, not a numerical restatement or arbitrary fixed parameter slice.
